briefing.opening: Good morning. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 11, 2026. Today, we will bring you updates on domestic and international efforts to address climate change, trends in renewable energy transition, and warnings about the deepening climate crisis.

sections.title: 🌍 Strengthening International Cooperation and Domestic Policies
sections.content: South Korea strengthened climate response cooperation with Malaysia by hosting the 4th Climate Change Conference, specifically discussing bioenergy cooperation using palm oil wastewater [1, 6, 7]. The UN Climate Change Executive Secretary emphasized that climate action is key to saving the economy, underscoring the importance of collective efforts [4]. Domestically, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) participated in negotiations for the Korea Green Economy Agreement, signaling its intent to lead new trade norms by actively discussing climate change response regulations [11, 20]. These developments align with international climate discussion platforms such as Climate Week NYC and the UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties (COP), and highlight the importance of global cooperation, including working-level meetings on nuclear and renewable energy between Vietnam and France [91, 101, 103].

sections.title: 🌱 Expanding Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Education
sections.content: Various domestic institutions and local governments are actively pursuing carbon neutrality practices. The Jeonnam Regional Headquarters of the Korea Rural Community Corporation is accelerating its climate change response through advanced digital disaster management [5]. Kumho E&C encouraged employee participation in carbon neutrality practices through its 'JUST WALK Season 5' walking challenge, achieving its highest participation rate ever [22, 23, 24, 33, 57, 58]. Seongnam City launched its 'Disposable-Free Public Office' challenge [25], while Changwon City gained recognition as an implementation-oriented model by achieving the top national performance for two consecutive years at the Jeju Carbon Neutrality stage [26]. Furthermore, the Gyeonggi Carbon Neutrality Support Center received an award for 'Excellent Local Government Carbon Neutrality Cases' [27, 42]. Cheonan City is also dedicated to environmental education for future generations, operating 'Visiting Carbon Neutrality Classrooms' for 2,884 students across 31 elementary and middle schools [28, 43, 48, 52, 54, 61, 62].

sections.title: 🔋 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Industry Trends
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating both domestically and internationally. The government has set a target of 100 GW of renewable energy by 2030 through the reconstruction of the solar industry [70], and a high public approval rate of 63% was observed for mandating renewable energy for mega-project power [64]. Local government efforts are also continuing, with Daejeon Dong-gu securing 1.22 billion KRW in national funding by achieving the highest 'A grade' in the 2027 Renewable Energy Convergence Support Project [65, 72, 81, 83]. Internationally, Albuquerque, USA, is pursuing 100% renewable energy for its administrative power by installing 6 MW of solar power in public facilities [68], and India's renewable energy capacity has expanded to the world's third-largest, indicating a clear global proliferation [71]. The Korea Food Industry Association and the Korea Energy Agency are collaborating to expand solar power and energy efficiency in the food industry [31, 36, 53, 75, 78, 84, 92], and discussions have also emerged that AI data centers could serve as a long-term catalyst for renewable energy expansion [79, 87].

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis Warnings and Calls for Action
sections.content: Globally, the severity of the climate crisis is being warned, and its impacts are becoming increasingly evident. The catastrophic floods in Nepal have been directly linked to climate change, leading to successive calls for establishing climate change damage prevention measures using satellites [14, 18, 98]. A research team led by Professor Jong-Seong Kug of Seoul National University warned that the Southern Ocean's carbon absorption capacity would be lost if carbon neutrality is delayed [21], and predictions indicate a fourfold increase in 'extreme heatwaves' within a few years [19]. New research has revealed that Canadian wildfires and permafrost thawing are further exacerbating climate change [102], and the aging U.S. water infrastructure has proven insufficient to cope with current climate changes [93]. Amidst these circumstances, there is criticism that wealthy nations are passing on an unbearable climate crisis bill to vulnerable countries like Nepal [94], alongside strong calls to vote for leaders who will address climate change [100].

briefing.closing: Today's news once again underscores the urgency of climate change response and the necessity of global cooperation. Everyone's efforts are crucial for a sustainable future. This concludes the climate briefing for September 11, 2026.
